title.en: Find probabilities with equally likely outcomes

say.en: Weather apps, cricket win predictors and board games all assign probabilities. Kolmogorov's three axioms are the rules that every one of them must follow. In this lesson: State the axioms of probability.
Find probabilities with equally likely outcomes.

body.en: A *probability* function P assigns to each event E a number such that (i) $P(E) \ge 0$; (ii) $P(S) = 1$; (iii) if E and F are mutually exclusive, $P(E \cup F) = P(E) + P(F)$. It follows that $P(\varnothing) = 0$, $0 \le P(E) \le 1$, and P(E) is the sum of the probabilities of the sample points in E.
body.kn: ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ ಎಂದಿಗೂ ಋಣವಲ್ಲ, P(S) = 1, ಮತ್ತು ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆಗಳು ಕೂಡುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Mutually exclusive: P(E ∪ F) = P(E) + P(F)

Throw two dice: 36 equally likely cells. The sum is 7 in the six green cells along a diagonal.
When outcomes are equally likely, the probability of an event is the number of favourable outcomes over the total: 6 over 36, one sixth.

body.en: If all $n$ outcomes of S are *equally likely*, each has probability $\frac1n$, and for any event E, $P(E) = \frac{n(E)}{n(S)}$. This is the classical definition of probability.
